title: Multicomponent Isotope Engineering of Phonon Polaritons in Hexagonal Boron Nitride
abstract: Isotopic enrichment provides a non-invasive means of tuning the vibrational and optical properties of van der Waals crystals (vdW) without altering their lattice structure. We investigate two doubly enriched hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) compositions, h10B15N and h11B15N, to determine how isotope substitution on both sublattices modifies mid-infrared hyperbolic phonon polaritons (HPhPs). Polarization-resolved room temperature and cryogenic far-field reflectance measurements reveal optical-phonon blue shifts of approximately 35 cm-1 in h10B15N relative h11B15N, translating both Reststrahlen bands (RBs) and their polariton dispersions. For the upper RB, the combined accessible range expands from 1360-1614 cm-1 in natural hBN to 1356-1640 cm-1 across the B- enriched 14N crystals and 1339-1640 cm-1 when the 15N enriched crystals are included. Near-field imaging confirms deeply sub-diffractional propagation and shows that both crystals exhibit lower polariton damping and longer lifetimes than natural hBN, with performance comparable to monoisotopically enriched crystals. Further, we compare the conventional reduced-mass description with a phenomenological two-component inverse-mass model that captures the isotope dependence of the phonon frequencies and LO-TO coupling while resolving the contributions of the individual sublattices. These results establish multicomponent isotope engineering as a materials design strategy for positioning the HPhPs spectral range while preserving low-loss propagation in polar vdW crystals.

summaries.en: Doubly isotope-enriched hexagonal boron nitride crystals (h10B15N and h11B15N) shift mid-infrared hyperbolic phonon polariton bands by about 35 cm-1, expand the accessible Reststrahlen range, and show lower polariton damping and longer lifetimes than natural hBN, establishing multicomponent isotope engineering as a route to tune polariton spectra while preserving low-loss propagation.
summaries.zh: 双同位素富集的六方氮化硼晶体（h10B15N 和 h11B15N）使中红外双曲声子极化激元带移动约 35 cm-1，拓展了可及 Reststrahlen 波段范围，并相比天然 hBN 表现出更低的极化激元阻尼和更长的寿命，从而确立了多组分同位素工程作为一种在保持低损耗传输的同时调控极化激元光谱的材料设计策略。
summaries.ja: 二重同位体濃縮した六方窒化ホウ素結晶（h10B15Nおよびh11B15N）は中赤外のハイパボリックフォノンポラリトン帯を約35 cm-1シフトさせ、利用可能なReststrahlen帯域を拡大するとともに、天然hBNより低いポラリトン減衰と長い寿命を示し、多成分同位体工学が低損失伝搬を保ちながらポラリトン分光域を制御する材料設計手法となることを確立した。

title: Optically modulated field-dependent electrical response in a non-collinear antiferromagnet/ferromagnet heterostructure
abstract: The interplay among optical, electrical, and magnetic stimuli offers opportunities to control the functional response of spintronic heterostructures. Here, we investigate the field-dependent electrical response of MgO/IrMn$_3$/Py/Au under radio-frequency (RF) excitation, white-light illumination, and direct-current (DC) bias. Under a 20 MHz RF signal with a nominal power of 2 W, the measured voltage in the dark remains at several tens of nanovolts. Upon illumination with approximately 1 W of white light, a pronounced field-dependent feature emerges around 315--320 Oe, reaching 0.9--1.0 $\mu$V. The illumination-associated differential voltage is approximately 0.95 $\mu$V. A DC current of 1 mA produces a response of approximately 1 $\mu$V, while the simultaneous application of RF, DC, and optical excitation increases the voltage to approximately 1.8 $\mu$V. Magnetic characterization reveals exchange bias with a blocking temperature near 380 K, while electrical resistance measurements show a pronounced dependence on magnetic-field orientation, consistent with the anisotropic response of the heterostructure. These results demonstrate that the field-dependent electrical response can be modulated through combined optical and electrical excitation, involving magneto-optical interactions and spin-dependent transport phenomena, potentially including spin Hall-related contributions and the magnetic spin Hall effect. This work provides insights into coupled optical, electrical, and magnetic-field effects in heterostructures based on non-collinear antiferromagnets and ferromagnetic layers.
subjects: Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall) ; Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci); Applied Physics (physics.app-ph); Optics (physics.optics)

summaries.en: White-light illumination, DC bias, and RF excitation are shown to jointly modulate a pronounced field-dependent voltage response around 315–320 Oe in a MgO/IrMn3/Py/Au non-collinear antiferromagnet/ferromagnet heterostructure, revealing coupled magneto-optical and spin-dependent transport effects.

title: Pair localization in one-dimensional quasicrystals with spin-dependent hopping
abstract: We investigate the quantum localization of two interacting particles moving in a one-dimensional quasicrystal with unequal hopping amplitudes. Using a two-body Green's function approach, we determine the localization phase diagram of attractively and repulsively bound pairs, showing that increasing the hopping amplitude of one constituent while keeping the other fixed raises the critical quasiperiodic strength, promoting pair delocalization. The localization threshold nevertheless remains bounded above by the Aubry-André critical point of the slower constituent. Effective analytical descriptions capture pair localization in the limits of strong hopping imbalance and strong interactions. The dynamics of an initially on-site pair provides signatures of delocalization induced by unequal hopping amplitudes. In particular, the effective spreading exponent of the root-mean-square width of a pair distribution reveals a progression from localized to subdiffusive and eventually superdiffusive behavior as the hopping ratio increases. Our results establish unequal hopping amplitudes as a means of tuning the transport properties of interacting pairs in quasiperiodic lattices, with direct relevance to ultracold atoms in optical lattices.
subjects: Quantum Gases (cond-mat.quant-gas) ; Disordered Systems and Neural Networks (cond-mat.dis-nn)

summaries.en: This study shows that unequal hopping amplitudes in a one-dimensional quasicrystal raise the critical quasiperiodic strength and promote delocalization of interacting pairs, with the localization threshold bounded by the Aubry-André critical point of the slower constituent and dynamics progressing from localized to subdiffusive to superdiffusive as the hopping ratio increases.

title: An infrared divacancy color center in bulk hexagonal diamond for quantum communication
abstract: Intrinsic color centers are investigated in bulk hexagonal diamond as potential emitters for fiber-based quantum communication. Hybrid density functional theory and constrained-occupation delta SCF calculations identify five carbon-vacancy and divacancy configurations with stable optical excited states. A comparison of their radiative and nonradiative properties within a three-point configuration-coordinate model identifies the positively charged axial divacancy, VVa1+, as the most promising candidate. It exhibits the highest calculated zero-phonon-line (ZPL) emission rate of 43.9 MHz and ZPL quantum efficiency of 11.8% among the five candidates. Its weak structural relaxation yields a Huang-Rhys factor of 0.395, while a multimode photoluminescence calculation gives a Debye-Waller factor of 69.37%, indicating a dominant zero-phonon contribution. The predicted ZPL at 0.603 eV (2057.3 nm) also has the smallest photon-energy separation from the 1310 and 1550 nm telecom targets among the candidates. These results identify VVa1+ as a promising intrinsic color center for fiber-based quantum communication, with quantum frequency upconversion offering a route from its strong infrared ZPL to the telecom O and C bands.

title: Chiral magnon Kerr interaction from linear and nonlinear Meissner screening in ferromagnet--superconductor bilayers
abstract: Magnon Kerr interaction showing a dependence of magnon dispersion frequency on its population is a useful functionality for nonlinear and quantum magnonics; its strength and sign depend on magnetic anisotropy, bias, and mode geometry. We here propose to use a superconducting gate to tune the Kerr interaction of magnons in ferromagnetic insulators. Even when the superconductor responds linearly, the frequency shift induced by its reflected dipolar field depends on the longitudinal magnetization. The decrease of this magnetization with increasing precession amplitude therefore produces a Kerr contribution. We go beyond this linear Meissner-screening regime by showing that at finite excitation amplitude, the significant Meissner screening currents reduce the superfluid stiffness, thus enhancing the effective magnetic-field penetration and rendering the Meissner backaction amplitude dependent. This superflow-induced pair breaking adds a second Kerr contribution, controlled by the interfacial superflow relative to the nonlinear screening scale. For yttrium iron garnet gated by dirty niobium, we predict a significant renormalization of the Kerr effect by superconductors, with the resulting Kerr contribution strongly chiral in the Damon--Eshbach configuration. By showing that the linear and nonlinear Meissner screening to the Kerr interaction can be distinguished by varying temperature, our work establishes a route to directional control of magnon nonlinear interactions.
subjects: Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall) ; Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

summaries.en: The paper predicts that a superconducting gate on a ferromagnetic insulator renormalizes the magnon Kerr interaction through two distinct contributions—a linear Meissner-screening term arising from the magnetization dependence of the reflected dipolar field and a nonlinear superflow-induced pair-breaking term that reduces superfluid stiffness—yielding a strongly chiral Kerr effect in the Damon-Eshbach configuration for yttrium iron garnet gated by dirty niobium.
summaries.zh: 该论文预测，铁磁绝缘体上的超导栅极通过两种不同机制重整化磁振子克尔相互作用——一种是由反射偶极场的磁化强度依赖产生的线性迈斯纳屏蔽项，另一种是降低超流刚度的非线性超流诱导配对破坏项——并在以脏铌为栅极的钇铁石榴石中，于Damon-Eshbach构型下产生强手性的克尔效应。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、強磁性絶縁体上の超伝導ゲートが、反射双極子場の磁化依存性に由来する線形マイスナー遮蔽項と超流体剛性を低下させる非線形超流誘起対破壊項という二つの寄与を通じてマグノンKerr相互作用を繰り込み、汚いニオブでゲートしたイットリウム鉄ガーネットにおいてDamon–Eshbach配置で強いカイラルなKerr効果を生み出すと予測している。

title: Frequency Comb as a Probe of Fluctuation Mechanisms in Nanomechanical Systems
abstract: Frequency combs are indispensable in metrology. We show that a frequency comb also probes frequency fluctuations of the system. In our nanomechanical resonator, the comb arises from self-sustained vibrations of a resonantly driven nonlinear mode. The comb lineshapes reveal exponentially correlated (Ornstein--Uhlenbeck) frequency noise. Its correlation time agrees with the independently measured relaxation time of the vibrations. The noise leads to anomalous phase diffusion. Its mechanism is generic: like the comb itself, it stems from the strong nonlinearity of the self-sustained vibrations.

summaries.en: Frequency comb lineshapes in a resonantly driven nonlinear nanomechanical resonator reveal exponentially correlated (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck) frequency noise whose correlation time matches the independently measured vibration relaxation time and produces anomalous phase diffusion, a mechanism generic to the strong nonlinearity of self-sustained vibrations.
summaries.zh: 在共振驱动的非线性纳米机械谐振器中，频率梳的谱线形状揭示了呈指数相关的（Ornstein-Uhlenbeck）频率噪声，其相关时间与独立测得的振动弛豫时间一致，并导致反常相位扩散，这一机制源于自持振动的强非线性，具有普遍性。
summaries.ja: 共振駆動された非線形ナノ機械共振器において、周波数コムの線形は指数関数的に相関する（オルンシュタイン・ウーレンベック）周波数雑音を明らかにし、その相関時間は独立に測定された振動の緩和時間と一致し、異常な位相拡散を引き起こす。

title: From Growth to Devices: Oxygen-Controlled Superconductivity in BSCCO Thin Films
abstract: Realizing device-compatible high-$T_c$ superconductors requires simultaneous control of oxygen stoichiometry and tolerance to nanofabrication. Here, we investigate sputtered Bi$_2$Sr$_2$Ca$_{n-1}$Cu$_n$O$_{2n+4+\delta}$ (BSCCO) thin films and establish a direct link between annealing conditions, oxygen incorporation, and superconducting transport. By independently varying the annealing temperature and duration, we identify an optimal annealing condition of $860\,^{\circ}$C for 3\,h, which yields the highest superconducting transition temperature and the narrowest transition among the investigated samples. X-ray diffraction, electron microscopy, and X-ray photoemission spectroscopy reveal a non-monotonic evolution of lattice oxygen, which governs hole doping in the CuO$_2$ planes and produces the characteristic dome-like dependence of $T_c$ on doping concentration. We further translate these optimized films into micro-devices to assess fabrication-induced effects, via micro-bridges as well as a planar Josephson junction. We demonstrate devices fabricated via both lift-off and focused ion beam (FIB) patterning methods -- proving the fabrication compatibility of these films. Importantly, we demonstrate their air-stability for extended periods of time (2 months). The combined insights offer practical guidelines for integrating cuprate thin films into superconducting electronics and quantum device architectures.

summaries.en: This study establishes that annealing conditions control oxygen stoichiometry and hole doping in sputtered BSCCO thin films, yielding an optimal 860 °C for 3 h treatment with the highest and narrowest superconducting transition, and demonstrates that these optimized films can be patterned into micro-bridges and planar Josephson junctions with air stability over two months.
summaries.zh: 本研究确立了溅射BSCCO薄膜的退火条件与氧化学计量及空穴掺杂之间的直接联系，发现860 °C退火3小时可获得最高且最窄的超导转变，并证明这些优化薄膜可被加工成微桥和平面约瑟夫森结，且在空气中稳定两个月。
summaries.ja: 本研究は、スパッタ成膜したBSCCO薄膜においてアニール条件が酸素化学量論とホールドーピングを制御することを示し、860 °C・3時間のアニールで最高かつ最もシャープな超伝導転移が得られ、最適化した薄膜がマイクロブリッジや平面ジョセフソン接合へ加工可能で、2か月間の大気安定性を持つことを実証した。

title: Nonreciprocal Josephson Dynamics of a $\mathcal{PT}$-Symmetric Atomtronic SQUID
abstract: We investigate non-Hermitian Josephson dynamics in an atomtronic quantum interference device (AQUID), formed by a ring Bose Einstein condensate with balanced atomic gain and loss regions and two moving optical barriers. The balanced gain and loss profile establishes a parity time symmetric potential while breaking spatial inversion symmetry, providing the essential ingredients for nonreciprocal Josephson transport. The dynamics are monitored nondestructively through the phase quadrature spectrum of an optomechanical cavity driven by Laguerre Gaussian beams coupled to the condensate. We demonstrate that increasing the local gain and loss strength softens the parity time symmetric collective mode towards an exceptional point, as verified by Bogoliubov de Gennes analysis. The associated coherent population exchange produces an additional characteristic splitting in the cavity output spectrum. For linearly translating barriers, non-Hermiticity provides an additional control parameter for tuning the critical current. When the barriers undergo simultaneous translation and rotation, the rotation induced phase modifies the interference between counter propagating currents, offering further control over the nonreciprocal response. Under periodic barrier modulation, we find more pronounced Shapiro steps in the current voltage characteristics due to the intrinsic parity time symmetric collective mode. Finally, we propose an alternative Hermitian realization using a tilted optical lattice, providing an experimentally accessible route to engineering biased transport and population transfer. Our results establish parity time symmetric atomtronic SQUIDs as a versatile platform for controlling nonreciprocal Josephson transport and collective excitations in driven quantum fluids.

summaries.en: The paper theoretically shows that a parity-time-symmetric atomtronic SQUID with balanced gain and loss exhibits nonreciprocal Josephson transport, tunable critical current, and enhanced Shapiro steps, with the dynamics read out via the phase quadrature spectrum of an optomechanical cavity.
summaries.zh: 该论文理论研究表明，具有平衡增益和损耗的宇称-时间对称原子电子SQUID表现出非互易约瑟夫森输运、可调临界电流和增强的Shapiro台阶，并通过光机械腔的相位正交谱进行非破坏性监测。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、平衡な利得と損失を持つパリティ時間対称なアトムトロニックSQUIDが非相反ジョセフソン輸送、調整可能な臨界電流、増強されたシャピロステップを示し、そのダイナミクスが光機械共振器の位相直交成分スペクトルを通じて非破壊的に観測されることを理論的に示した。

title: Good Practices for Measuring the Interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction by Brillouin Light Scattering and Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect
abstract: The interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (iDMI) is a key ingredient for stabilizing chiral magnetic states, such as skyrmions and chiral domain walls, which are key building blocks for next-generation spintronic technologies. Despite its importance, the quantitative determination of the iDMI constant, $D$, is often plagued by significant discrepancies. This paper establishes a set of good practices for measuring iDMI using two primary techniques: Brillouin Light Scattering (BLS) and the Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect (MOKE). Through the analysis of Co/Pt-based heterostructures, this work provides a comprehensive roadmap for measurement procedures, data evaluation, and uncertainty analysis. Our analysis highlights the crucial role of magnetic parameters used to extract the iDMI constant and propagation of their uncertainties, and the measurement model for enhancing measurement reliability. The proposed methodology provides a practical framework for improving the consistency and reproducibility of iDMI measurements across different laboratories and experimental techniques.

summaries.en: This paper establishes good practices for measuring the interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction using Brillouin Light Scattering and the Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect, providing a roadmap for measurement procedures, data evaluation, and uncertainty analysis that emphasizes the role of magnetic parameters and the measurement model in improving consistency and reproducibility across laboratories and techniques.
summaries.zh: 本文提出了使用布里渊光散射和磁光克尔效应测量界面Dzyalinskii-Moriya相互作用的最佳实践，为测量流程、数据评估和不确定性分析提供了全面路线图，强调了磁参数及其不确定性传播以及测量模型在提高不同实验室和实验技术间测量一致性与可重复性方面的关键作用。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、ブリルアン光散乱と磁気光学カー効果を用いた界面ジャロシンスキー・守谷相互作用の測定に関するグッドプラクティスを確立し、測定手順・データ評価・不確かさ解析のためのロードマップを提供するとともに、iDMI定数の抽出に用いる磁気パラメータとその不確かさの伝播、および測定モデルが測定の信頼性を高める上で果たす重要な役割を強調している。

title: Tuning and Mapping of Two-Tone Optomechanical Instability up to the Physical Limits
abstract: We report on the compete theory describing the two-tone instability proper to optomechanical back-action-evading experiments. We address all possible mistunings (including power imbalance of the two pumps), as well as the device imperfections (finite mechanical quality factor, and sideband resolution). We illustrate the importance of power mistuning and sideband resolution, the latter being particularly relevant in finding the back-action-evading "sweet spot". The model is compared to experiments performed up to an extremely high cooperativity, of almost a 100. This has been made possible thanks to a fine-tuning procedure, which is presented. The agreement theory-experiment is very good, and the limiting factor is unraveled: cavity frequency noise. Besides, we discover at very high drive powers new self-driven states, which all share the characteristic feature of presenting a mechanical comb spectrum; as if the synchronization of the responses to the two drives (which occurs at lower powers) was destroyed by nonlinear effects. We believe that our work is extremely relevant to the implementation of back-action-evading experiments, as well as other related two-tone schemes.

summaries.en: The paper presents a complete theory of two-tone optomechanical instability covering all mistunings, power imbalance, finite mechanical quality factor, and sideband resolution, validated against experiments up to a cooperativity of nearly 100, revealing cavity frequency noise as the limiting factor and discovering new self-driven mechanical comb states at very high drive powers.
summaries.zh: 本文提出了双音光机械不稳定性的完整理论，涵盖所有失谐、功率不平衡、有限机械品质因子和边带分辨率，并在高达近100的协同度下与实验吻合良好，揭示腔频率噪声是限制因素，并发现极高驱动功率下出现具有机械梳状频谱的新自驱动态。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、全ての離調、ポンプ間のパワー不均衡、有限の機械的品質因子、サイドバンド分解能を含む二トーン光機械不安定性の完全な理論を提示し、協同度がほぼ100に達する実験と良好に一致して空洞周波数雑音が制限要因であることを明らかにするとともに、非常に高い駆動電力で機械コムスペクトルを持つ新たな自己駆動状態を発見した。

title: EoSAlign: An Open-Source Software for Calculating, Comparing, and Aligning Pressure Under Extreme Conditions
abstract: Accurate pressure determination is essential in high pressure experiments. Inconsistencies among pressure scales limit direct comparisons and contribute to uncertainty in measured properties, such as, phase boundaries, melting conditions, and thermodynamic models, especially above 100 GPa where existing scales diverge by >10 GPa. EoSAlign, an open-source software, can calculate, compare, and align pressures using a range of published calibrations. EoSAlign calculates pressure from experimental measurements (such as volume (A^3), Raman shift (cm^-1), or luminescence peak position (nm)) and it can be used to compare pressure values from different pressure standards. Using EoSAlign, we fit and align the bridgmanite and post-perovskite equations of state to a common scale, enabling us to reduce pressure scale related differences. EoSAlign can be applied to any high pressure data analysis to compare experimental results, improve consistency between studies, and advance our understanding of planetary interiors and high pressure physics.
subjects: Geophysics (physics.geo-ph) ; Earth and Planetary Astrophysics (astro-ph.EP); Instrumentation and Methods for Astrophysics (astro-ph.IM); Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

summaries.en: EoSAlign is an open-source software that calculates, compares, and aligns pressures under extreme conditions using a range of published calibrations, enabling consistent pressure determinations across different scales for high-pressure data analysis.
summaries.zh: EoSAlign是一个开源软件，利用多种已发表的校准方法计算、比较并对齐极端条件下的压力，从而实现不同压力标度间的一致压力测定，以用于高压数据分析。
summaries.ja: EoSAlignは、公開されている様々な校正法を用いて極限環境下の圧力を計算・比較・整合するオープンソースソフトウェアであり、異なる圧力スケール間で一貫した圧力決定を可能にし、高圧データ解析に活用できる。

title: Development of a Long-Term Stable Three-Axis Single-Beam Vector Optically Pumped Magnetometer Using a Buffer-Gas-Free Rubidium Vapor Cell and Direct Absorption Frequency Locking for Unshielded Geomagnetic Monitoring
abstract: Optically pumped magnetometers (OPMs) achieve ultra-high sensitivity, yet sustaining long-term stability in unshielded, dynamic geomagnetic environments remains challenging. Here, we present the design and unshielded validation of a three-axis vector OPM achieving sub-nanotesla accuracy using an off-the-shelf rubidium (Rb) ampoule and a vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL). Unlike conventional sensors, this system operates without high-pressure buffer gases, mitigating wall-collision relaxation via a single-beam geometry combined with active zero-field nulling and adiabatic 70 kHz AC heating. To suppress VCSEL thermal wavelength drift without sub-Doppler optics, active frequency stabilization based on direct absorption spectroscopy (DAS) was implemented across a wide capture range. Continuous evaluation in an unshielded laboratory in Okayama against synthetic geomagnetic records from the Kakioka and Kanoya observatories demonstrated exceptional horizontal tracking fidelity. Concurrently, the vertical transfer matrix resolved the regional geomagnetic coast effect, extracting Parkinson induction vectors reflecting regional conductivity contrast, with high robustness against DC electric railway interference. Spectral characterization showed an intrinsic white noise floor of 10-20 pT above 1 Hz, enhanced by digital oversampling beyond the 12-bit DAC quantization limit, while residual overlapped Allan deviation revealed a 0.1 nT bias instability at 100-200 s integration times. These results prove that a compact, low-cost OPM platform based on commercial components can suppress long-term drift and serve as a reliable instrument for geophysical surveys and unshielded magnetic sensing.

title: Background-free and laser-ionization minimized single-shot fs-EFISH in luminous pulsed plasmas
abstract: This work introduces spectrally tuned electric field induced second harmonic (t-EFISH) generation for substantially reducing or eliminating background plasma emission in single-shot, time-resolved, electric field measurements. The technique is demonstrated using a femtosecond 1240 nm pump and 620 nm signal detection to avoid spectral and temporal overlap with the early, intense onset of N2(C-B) emission in nanosecond atmospheric-pressure air spark discharges. This enhances signal-to-emission ratios pre- and post-breakdown, enables lower pump energies, suppresses detector saturation, and reduces the coefficient of variation in the electric field measurements by 8.5x. This strategy also provides a pathway for background-free measurements in other discharge environments with varying spectro-temporal emission characteristics. Moreover, the longer 1240 nm pump wavelength reduces multiphoton intrusiveness, directly improving measurement fidelity.

title: Molecular Gas Optics Using Vibrational Population Density Refraction
abstract: Gas optics holds promise for development of advanced optical elements with 2-3 orders of magnitude higher damage threshold than any solid-state optics. Here, we demonstrate a new concept for refracting the laser beam using vibrationally excited molecules as gas optics instead of traditional control of thermodynamic gas temperature. The transient, vibrational population density grating is formed in a CO2 gas by interfering two mid-IR lasers to imprint spatial modulation in the linear refractive index (Delta n0 >=2x10-5) of the neutral gas via enhancement of the molecular polarizability. It is increased by pumping the asymmetric stretching mode of CO2 at optimal wavelengths to resonantly produce a highly nonequilibrium state that increases the effective vibrational mode temperature to greater than 2000 K in a room temperature gas. The measured beam steering efficiency of such a volume gas grating exceeds 90% that makes this approach a candidate for producing other large-aperture, high-throughput molecular optics elements, with expected damage thresholds 0.5-1 kJ/cm2, much-needed for future ultrahigh-power lasers.

summaries.en: A transient vibrational population density grating formed in CO2 gas by interfering mid-IR lasers creates a spatial modulation of the linear refractive index (Delta n0 >= 2x10-5) via enhanced molecular polarizability, achieving beam steering efficiency exceeding 90% and offering a pathway to large-aperture molecular gas optics with expected damage thresholds of 0.

title: Hysteresis and mode switching in FIB engineered random laser diodes
abstract: Complex dynamical behavior in laser diodes is commonly induced by external perturbations such as optical or optoelectronic feedback and optical injection. The structural transformation of a stable laser diode into a stand-alone nonlinear dynamical system would provide a practical alternative as a single and compact device. Here we demonstrate the fabrication of such a device by milling, via focused ion beam, the output facet of a Fabry-Perot laser diode with a predesigned mask, obtaining a scattering surface which provide feedback for random lasing. The fabricated random laser diode shows multi-mode emission with current dependent spectral reconfigurations, hysteresis in output power and spectrum and mode switching at constant bias current. We attribute this behavior to the interplay between scattered optical feedback and carrier induced local variations of refractive index and temperature at the output facet surface, where defects are located. The observed phenomena reveal complex nonlinear behavior emerging from a single standalone device, which could be tailored by varying the milling pattern, thereby providing a flexible platform for different applications.

summaries.en: Focused ion beam milling of a Fabry-Perot laser diode facet with a predesigned mask creates a scattering surface that provides optical feedback, turning the device into a stand-alone random laser diode that exhibits current-dependent spectral reconfigurations, hysteresis in output power and spectrum, and mode switching at constant bias current due to the interplay of scattered feedback, carrier-induced refractive index variations, and temperature effects at the facet defects.

title: Universal spectral shapes of nonlinear light scattering from laser-driven dilute-gas density gratings
abstract: Operating within the framework of the collisionless Boltzmann equation, we identify universal spectral profiles inherent in stimulated and coherent light scattering from laser-driven dilute-gas density gratings and derive physically intuitive solutions for such spectral shapes, expressing them in a manifestly causal closed form that satisfies the Kramers - Kronig relations and fulfills the fluctuation - dissipation theorem. Benchmarking against gold-standard experiments on dilute-gas stimulated light scattering verifies a high descriptive and explanatory power of these solutions and demonstrates their ability to isolate universality motifs in nonlinear scattering spectra as the key to fully understanding the physics behind dilute-gas nonlinear light scattering. As one of important outcomes, such analysis reveals the physical content of the bandwidth of dilute-gas nonlinear scattering spectra as an expression and a quantifier of the phase-mixing time, i.e., the time required for free-streaming gas particles with a mean thermal velocity to traverse the distance equal to the spacing of the laser-driven density grating.

summaries.en: Working from the collisionless Boltzmann equation, the authors derive causal, Kramers-Kronig-consistent, fluctuation-dissipation-satisfying closed-form solutions for the universal spectral profiles of stimulated and coherent light scattering from laser-driven dilute-gas density gratings, validated against gold-standard experiments, which identify the spectral bandwidth as a quantifier of the phase-mixing time set by the thermal traversal of the grating spacing.
summaries.zh: 作者从无碰撞玻尔兹曼方程出发，推导出激光驱动的稀薄气体密度光栅所产生的受激与相干光散射的普适谱形的因果闭式解，该解满足Kramers-Kronig关系和涨落-耗散定理，并与稀薄气体受激光散射的基准实验相符，由此揭示谱带宽可量化相位混合时间，即平均热速度的气体粒子自由飞行穿过密度光栅间距所需的时间。

title: Compact plasma-based extreme compression of relativistic electron beams
abstract: Accelerated particle beams are essential tools of modern science and technology with applications ranging from medicine [1], to light sources [2], to high-energy physics [3]. Over time, as accelerator-based experiments become more sophisticated and probe natural phenomena with greater temporal resolution, there is an increasing demand on beam parameters, in particular on bunch duration. Experiments have been proposed that require beams with 1-2 orders of magnitude shorter durations than what is possible with current state-of-the-art technology. However, state-of-the-art temporal bunch compressors force a trade-off between how short an electron bunch can be made and how well its transverse quality survives the strong bending magnets required to do so -- a limitation that stands as a grand challenge for accelerator physics to-date [4]. In this experiment, we demonstrate a new, compact compression technique for generating ultrashort, high-peak-current electron bunches that circumvents this trade-off using plasma wakefield acceleration. Just as chirped pulse amplification unlocked ultrashort, high-power laser pulses and the technologies that followed from them, here we demonstrate an analogous chirp-and-compress strategy applied to relativistic electron beams by using the extreme electric fields of a plasma wakefield in place of a stretcher-amplifier, thereby unlocking the path to ultrashort, extremely high-current electron beams. We demonstrate the first application of this plasma-compressed bunch using it to drive single-microbunch free electron lasing at optical wavelengths in a single, meter-scale undulator module, producing radiation pulses roughly four orders of magnitude more energetic than the first beam-driven, plasma-based free electron laser demonstration at the same accelerator facility [5, 6].

summaries.en: Using plasma wakefield acceleration, researchers demonstrated a compact chirp-and-compress technique that generates ultrashort, high-peak-current relativistic electron bunches without sacrificing transverse beam quality, and used these bunches to drive single-microbunch free-electron lasing at optical wavelengths with pulses about four orders of magnitude more energetic than an earlier plasma-based free-electron laser at the same facility.

title: Hopfion Superlattices in 3D Twisted Moiré Light Fields
abstract: Moiré superlattices have recently been extended from electronic materials to photonic systems, enabling complex topological light fields such as skyrmion bags. However, these realizations remain confined to two dimensions. Here, we demonstrate 3D moiré superlattices formed by twisting multi-volume spatiotemporal optical lattices, giving rise to previously undiscovered 3D quasiparticle topologies, including hopfion bags, hopfion quasicrystals, and hopfion-hopfionium nested superlattices. By tailoring the interference polarization textures of the moiré spacetime lattices, we achieve controlled topological transitions among these states, and tailored topological numbers of hopfion bags. These spatiotemporal supertopologies offer a promising platform for high-capacity information encoding in higher dimensions.

summaries.en: By twisting multi-volume spatiotemporal optical lattices, the authors create three-dimensional moiré superlattices that host previously unobserved quasiparticle topologies such as hopfion bags, hopfion quasicrystals, and nested hopfion-hopfionium superlattices, with controlled topological transitions and tailored topological numbers enabling high-capacity information encoding.

title: Development of a versatile modular system to study the ablation and plume expansion in a thin film
abstract: Time-resolved investigation of laser ablation of thin films requires stable, repeatable, and efficient experimental environment. Conventional approaches often rely on multiple laser-ablation shots acquired at different delay times to reconstruct the temporal evolution of the process, thereby assuming shot-to-shot reproducibility. This work presents a novel modular experimental setup that addresses these challenges and enables a systematic pump--probe study of laser--matter interaction. The setup provides reliable single-pulse measurements with controlled sample positioning inside the high vacuum chamber, as well as integrated data recording, which improves redundancy and ease with which experiments can be performed. Further, the setup serves as an advanced diagnostic tool for investigating the time evolution of laser--matter interactions, ablation dynamics and laser-produced plasmas in a single laser shot, in various configurations with a temporal resolution better than 15 ns. Using this capability, we show that for a fixed ablation geometry, the transient reflectivity and transmission response depends strongly on the probing side, indicating that probing direction is an independent diagnostic variable whose omission can lead to incomplete or misleading picture of the ablation dynamics. This experimental technique can advance the understanding of surface modification and plume expansion, which are relevant to fundamental studies and also for range of applications, including laser cleaning of tokamak viewports and mirrors, pulsed laser deposition (PLD), surface structuring and laser-induced forward transfer (LIFT), among others. The present setup is versatile enough to perform these studies under different ablation configurations without implementing major changes in the experimental configuration.
subjects: Optics (physics.optics) ; Instrumentation and Detectors (physics.ins-det); Plasma Physics (physics.plasm-ph)

summaries.en: The paper presents a versatile modular high-vacuum pump–probe setup that enables reliable single-shot, time-resolved measurements of thin-film laser ablation and plume expansion with sub-15-ns temporal resolution, and shows that transient reflectivity and transmission depend strongly on the probing side, making probe direction an independent diagnostic variable.
summaries.zh: 本文介绍了一种通用的模块化高真空泵浦-探测装置，能够在优于15纳秒的时间分辨率下可靠地进行单发、时间分辨的薄膜激光烧蚀与羽流膨胀测量，并表明瞬态反射率和透射率强烈依赖于探测方向，因此探测方向是一个独立的诊断变量。

title: Revisiting the dispersions and quality factors of nanoshell plasmons
abstract: The dispersions and quality factors of a metallic nanoshell's plasmons may be readily tuned by varying the thickness of the nanoshell. This is because 1. Thickness determines the hybridization between the two nanoshell boundaries and 2. Thickness affects the electronic surface scattering rate and, therefore, the non-radiative decay rates of the plasmonic resonances. We find that prior theoretical works, focused primarily on the thin-nanoshell and retarded regimes, obtained qualitatively incorrect results for both the plasmonic dispersions and the associated plasmonic quality factors. Some of these errors have been pointed out in subsequent works, though the corrected results have not been reported, to our knowledge. Beyond obtaining the correct results (correct dispersions and quality factors as a function of nanoshell thickness), we scrutinize the assumption (used by many prior works) that Matthiessen's rule may be used to combine the effects of bulk and surface-mediated plasmonic scattering processes. To do so, we extend prior work by Dingle to the nanoshell geometry. Although we find qualitative agreement with the Matthiessen's rule approach, we find that Dingle's theory systematically predicts higher quality factors across the range of nanoshell thicknesses we consider.

summaries.en: Correcting prior theoretical errors, this study derives the plasmon dispersions and quality factors of metallic nanoshells as functions of shell thickness and, by extending Dingle's theory to the nanoshell geometry, finds that Dingle's approach systematically predicts higher quality factors than the Matthiessen's-rule treatment despite qualitative agreement.
summaries.zh: 本研究纠正了以往理论中的错误，给出了金属纳米壳等离激元色散与品质因数随壳层厚度变化的正确结果，并将Dingle理论推广到纳米壳几何结构，发现尽管与马西森定则方法在定性上一致，但Dingle理论在所考察的壳层厚度范围内系统性地预测出更高的品质因数。
summaries.ja: 本研究は従来の理論的誤りを修正し、金属ナノシェルのプラズモン分散と品質因子をシェル厚の関数として正しく導出するとともに、Dingleの理論をナノシェル形状に拡張し、Matthiessenの規則による取り扱いと定性的には一致するものの、検討したシェル厚の範囲全体でDingleの理論が系統的に高い品質因子を予測することを見出した。

title: Overcoming Dynamic Range Limitations in Computational Hyperspectral Imaging
abstract: Computational hyperspectral imaging offers compact spectral sensing, yet imaging high-dynamic-range (HDR) scenes remains challenging. Accurate spectral reconstruction requires encoded measurements to remain within the calibrated linear-response range and above the noise floor. Due to unequal spectral responsivities across the encoding mask, individual channels reach their reliability limits at vastly different incident signal levels. Measurement reliability therefore depends on both exposure time and encoding channel, making it challenging for a single exposure to preserve spectral information in highlights and shadows simultaneously. Here, we demonstrate a physics-guided multi-exposure fusion framework that operates directly in the encoded measurement domain. An analytical reliability prior and learned spatially varying, channel-specific adjustments jointly determine adaptive fusion weights. Measurement-domain spectral-angle supervision further constrains relative channel responses for downstream spectral inversion. The set-wise formulation accommodates varying numbers and configurations of input exposures. We further implement the framework on a 9-channel broadband-encoded stochastic hyperspectral camera, incorporating full-field sensor-response characterization and channel-aware reliability gating. Simulated HDR benchmarks show lower reconstruction errors than representative fusion methods, while controlled spectral measurements and practical HDR scenes confirm improved spectral fidelity and extended usable dynamic range. Measurements using an optical-density target further establish a 16.0-dB increase in spectral reconstruction dynamic range relative to the best fixed single exposure.

summaries.en: A physics-guided multi-exposure fusion framework operating in the encoded measurement domain, combining an analytical reliability prior with learned channel-specific adjustments and measurement-domain spectral-angle supervision, extends the usable dynamic range of a 9-channel broadband-encoded stochastic hyperspectral camera by 16.

title: Stress-controlled avoided-crossing evolution of an optical microresonator induced by inter-fibre side coupling
abstract: Analogies between quantum mechanics and photonics provide a powerful means of transferring concepts and phenomena between the two fields. Photonic analogues offer a distinctive advantage by allowing us to engineer and continuously vary parameters fixed by the microscopic structure of quantum systems, revealing richer behaviour. Building on these analogies, the recent demonstration of widely tunable microresonators formed by side coupling between optical fibres marked a significant advance in the development of reconfigurable resonant photonic systems. However, those methods offered no direct way to reach the centre of the avoided crossing, where the uncoupled fibre cutoff frequencies coincide and the modes hybridise most strongly. Here, we introduce an additional tuning degree of freedom by axially stretching a straight fibre coupled to a bent fibre. At essentially fixed coupling geometry, this lets us sweep the detuning between their uncoupled cutoff frequencies through zero. As the avoided crossing is approached, the induced microresonator's resonance band widens. Beyond the crossing, the band narrows and, strikingly, appears to "hang" below the stretched fibre's rising cutoff frequency. Our experimental results agree with coupled-mode theory and indicate the feasibility of 100 MHz-scale control of the straight-fibre cutoff frequency and the resonator spectral height over a tuning range of about 100 GHz, using a relative elongation of order $10^{-3}$.

summaries.en: By axially stretching a straight optical fibre coupled to a bent fibre, the detuning between their uncoupled cutoff frequencies can be swept through zero at essentially fixed coupling geometry, allowing stress-controlled access to the centre of the avoided crossing where the induced microresonator's resonance band widens and, beyond the crossing, narrows while appearing to hang below the stretched fibre's rising cutoff frequency, in agreement with coupled-mode theory.
summaries.zh: 通过轴向拉伸与弯曲光纤耦合的直光纤，可在基本固定的耦合几何下使两者未耦合截止频率之间的失谐扫过零点，从而以应力控制方式到达避免交叉的中心，在此处诱导微谐振器的共振带变宽，而越过交叉点后共振带变窄并显著地似乎悬于拉伸光纤上升的截止频率之下，结果与耦合模理论一致。
summaries.ja: 曲げたファイバーと結合した直線ファイバーを軸方向に伸長することで、結合幾何をほぼ固定したまま両者の非結合カットオフ周波数間の離調をゼロまで掃引でき、誘起マイクロ共振器の共鳴帯が広がる回避交差の中心へ応力制御で到達できること、また交差を越えると共鳴帯が狭まり伸長したファイバーの上昇するカットオフ周波数の下方に「ぶら下がる」ように見えることを、結合モード理論と一致する実験結果として示した。

title: Time-Varying Photonics: A Review of Theory, Phenomena, and Experimental Platforms
abstract: Time-varying photonics opens new avenues for controlling waves through engineering material properties in time. In this review, we introduce the basic concepts and theoretical tools for describing temporal interfaces, time-periodic systems, and space-time media, as well as review representative experimental approaches across different photonic and wave platforms. We further discuss characteristic phenomena enabled by temporal modulation, including coherent wave control, parametric amplification, nonreciprocity, and topological effects. This review provides a unified pathway for understanding time-varying photonics and outlines its current challenges and future opportunities in both fundamental physics and practical applications.

summaries.en: This review presents the theoretical tools, representative experimental platforms, and characteristic phenomena of time-varying photonics, including temporal interfaces, time-periodic systems, and space-time media that enable coherent wave control, parametric amplification, nonreciprocity, and topological effects.
summaries.zh: 本综述介绍了时变光子学的理论工具、代表性实验平台和特征现象，涵盖时间界面、时间周期系统和时空介质，这些机制可实现相干波控制、参量放大、非互易性和拓扑效应。
summaries.ja: 本レビューは、時間界面・時間周期的系・時空間媒体を含む時変フォトニクスの理論的枠組み、代表的な実験プラットフォーム、およびコヒーレント波制御・パラメトリック増幅・非相反性・トポロジカル効果といった特徴的現象を概説する。

title: Additively manufactured ceramic platforms for miniaturized optical frequency references and robust atomic sensor systems
abstract: Transferring atomic quantum sensors from laboratory-scale physics packages to compact, alignment-free sensor heads suitable for field and space deployment requires a structural platform that combines mechanical, thermal, and optical functionality within a single, manufacturable component. We present such a platform based on additively manufactured technical ceramics: lithography-based ceramic manufacturing is used to fabricate monolithic micro-optical benches with application-specific mounting geometries, while high-precision active alignment and adhesive bonding realize long-term stable optical assemblies through micro-integration. As a first system-level demonstrator, we present a micro-integrated optical frequency reference based on Doppler-free spectroscopy of the rubidium D2 line, integrated within a 6 mL Al2O3 module. A laser stabilized to the reference reaches a fractional frequency instability of $3\times10^{-12}$ at 1 s. We extend the platform to a compact optically pumped magnetometer, exploiting the magnetic cleanliness and tailored thermal properties of high-purity ceramics for a 7 mL sensor head with picotesla sensitivity aimed at space-borne biomagnetometry, and to a micro-integrated optical dipole trap with active MEMS-mirror beam steering for cold-atom manipulation. Together, these demonstrators show that ceramic additive manufacturing and optical micro-integration form a versatile, robust platform for compact atomic sensor systems in field and space applications.

summaries.en: Additively manufactured technical ceramics enable monolithic micro-optical benches with active alignment and adhesive bonding, demonstrated in a 6 mL rubidium-based optical frequency reference reaching a fractional instability of 3×10^-12 at 1 s and extended to a 7 mL optically pumped magnetometer with picotesla sensitivity and a MEMS-steered optical dipole trap for cold-atom manipulation.
summaries.zh: 增材制造技术陶瓷结合主动对准与粘接微集成，实现了单片微光学平台，并在6 mL铷D2线无多普勒光谱光学频率参考中达到1 s处3×10^-12的频率不稳定度，同时扩展至具有皮特斯拉灵敏度的7 mL光泵磁力计以及用于冷原子操控的MEMS反射镜光束扫描光偶极阱。
summaries.ja: 付加製造技術セラミックスと能動アライメント・接着接合による光マイクロ集積を用いてモノリシック微小光学ベンチを実現し、6 mLのルビジウムD2線ドップラーなし分光に基づく光周波数基準で1秒時に3×10^-12の周波数不安定性を達成するとともに、ピコテスラ感度を持つ7 mL光ポンピング磁力計やMEMSミラー走査による冷原子操作用光双極子トラップへと展開した。

title: An Alignment Microscope for Imaging Rotational Wavepacket Dynamics
abstract: We introduce a new method for encoding polarization-angle-dependent molecular alignment signals directly into the transverse spatial profile of a femtosecond laser beam. The approach employs a pump-probe setup in a common-path geometry. A radial-azimuthal polarization converter placed in the probe beam produces a doughnut-shaped beam whose local polarization varies continuously with azimuthal angle, thereby encoding the full range of linear polarization orientations from 0 to $2\pi$ within a single transverse beam profile. Consequently, the angular dependence of the molecular response can be recorded simultaneously rather than reconstructed through sequential measurements at different polarization angles. By varying only the pump-probe delay, this spatial encoding enables single-shot acquisition of the complete angular response at each delay and real-time visualization of the evolving molecular alignment pattern as the delay stage is scanned. This technique has enabled the experimental realization of an alignment microscope.

summaries.en: A new alignment microscope encodes polarization-angle-dependent molecular alignment signals into the transverse spatial profile of a femtosecond probe beam using a radial-azimuthal polarization converter, enabling single-shot acquisition of the full angular response and real-time visualization of rotational wavepacket dynamics.
summaries.zh: 一种新的对准显微镜利用径向-方位角偏振转换器将依赖偏振角的分子对准信号编码到飞秒探测光束的横向空间分布中，从而能够单次采集完整的角度响应并实时可视化旋转波包动力学。
summaries.ja: 新しいアラインメント顕微鏡は、ラジアル-アジマサル偏光変換器を用いて偏光角依存の分子アラインメント信号をフェムト秒プローブビームの横空間プロファイルにエンコードし、完全な角度応答の単発取得と回転波束ダイナミクスのリアルタイム可視化を可能にする。

title: Two atoms with strong light-induced dipolar interactions
abstract: We study how two atoms scatter light when they are closer than an optical wavelength and observe multiple new phenomena due to the strong interactions between laser-induced electric dipole moments. We identify a narrow range of densities where a fraction of the scattered light is coherent and shows a collective enhancement factor of two compared to independent atoms. The dynamics of the two-atom wavefunction can be observed through momentum distributions which reveal resonant ejection and depletion. Due to the tight confinement, the total fluorescence intensity strongly depends on the scattering length, since it originates from a narrow resonant (Franck-Condon) region. Furthermore, we measure how the probe laser intensity modifies the scattering length, which establishes a new way to shift Feshbach resonances. Our work provides microscopic insight into what occurs during photoassociation and parity projection in optical tweezers.

summaries.en: Two closely spaced atoms with strong light-induced dipolar interactions exhibit collective light scattering with a twofold enhancement, resonant ejection and depletion visible in momentum distributions, scattering-length-dependent fluorescence from a narrow Franck-Condon region, and a probe-intensity-induced shift of Feshbach resonances, offering microscopic insight into photoassociation and parity projection in optical tweezers.
summaries.zh: 两个间距小于光波长的原子在强光致偶极相互作用下表现出多种新现象，包括散射光中一部分相干成分具有相比独立原子两倍的集体增强、通过动量分布可观测到的共振弹射与耗尽、源于狭窄弗兰克-康登区域且强烈依赖散射长度的总荧光强度，以及探测激光强度对散射长度的调制所实现的新费什巴赫共振移动方式，从而为光镊中的光缔合与宇称投影提供了微观洞察。
summaries.ja: 光波長より近接した二原子が強い光誘起双極子相互作用のもとで、独立原子比で2倍の集団的増強を示すコヒーレント散乱、運動量分布に現れる共鳴的放出と枯渇、狭いフランク・コンドン領域に由来し散乱長に強く依存する全蛍光強度、さらにプローブレーザー強度による散乱長の変化を通じた新たなファインバッハ共鳴シフトなど複数の新現象を示し、光ピンセットにおける光会合とパリティ射影の微視的理解を与える。

title: SGAA: Independent active alignment of optical subgroups with uncompensated aberrations
abstract: Uncompensated subgroup aberrations complicate subgroup-level active alignment (AA), as local image-quality extrema do not directly indicate the target alignment state. We propose SGAA, an image-learning-based method for independent active alignment of optical subgroups. Multi-field point spread functions (PSFs) from a dedicated test configuration characterize misalignment, while golden-sample reference calibration and unified regression predict adjustments toward a common optical target across toleranced specimens. In simulations with tolerances, one step reduced the mean differential wavefront RMS from $0.0592\lambda$ to $0.0086\lambda$, an 85.4% reduction. In alignment experiments on 100 production subgroups, SGAA increased the mean full-lens weighted modulation transfer function (WMTF) at 30, 50, and 80 lp/mm by 0.073, 0.065, and 0.040, respectively, relative to industrial MTF-based scanning. The 8 MP acceptance yield increased by 29.2 percentage points, and mean alignment time decreased from 43 s to 3.1 s. SGAA thus translates independent subgroup reference-state restoration into gains in full-lens imaging, acceptance yield, and alignment speed.

summaries.en: SGAA is an image-learning-based method that uses multi-field point spread functions from a dedicated test configuration, golden-sample reference calibration, and unified regression to independently align optical subgroups despite uncompensated aberrations, reducing mean differential wavefront RMS by 85.
summaries.zh: SGAA是一种基于图像学习的光学子组独立主动对准方法，它利用专用测试配置下的多视场点扩散函数、金样参考标定和统一回归来克服未补偿像差的影响，在仿真中将平均差分波前RMS降低85.
summaries.ja: SGAAは、専用テスト構成からの多視野点像分布関数、ゴールデンサンプル参照校正、統一回帰を用いて未補償収差があっても光学的サブグループを独立に能動整列する画像学習ベースの手法であり、シミュレーションで平均差動波面RMSを85.

title: Physics-informed Bayesian optimization of high-order harmonic generation in gases
abstract: Optimization of high-order harmonic generation in gases is essential for attosecond science. Improving conversion efficiency from the infrared driving laser to the extreme-ultraviolet high-order harmonic radiation requires balancing microscopic single-atom dipole responses with macroscopic phase matching. The resulting conversion-efficiency landscape exhibits complex structures, such as the hyperbolic ridge in the pressure-length space, which can be difficult to accurately reconstruct using conventional Bayesian optimization. Here, we introduce a physics-informed Bayesian optimization framework that incorporates known physical scaling relations through nonlinear transformations of the search space. We first demonstrate the approach in the two-dimensional pressure-length space, where a direct grid scan enables detailed validation of the reconstructed landscape, before extending it to four dimensions, where exhaustive scanning becomes computationally impractical. In four dimensions, incorporating the pulse-duration scaling and a square-root transformation of conversion efficiency further improves the accuracy of the reconstructed landscape, as validated against an independent reference dataset. We also employ a threshold-based acquisition strategy to identify extended high-efficiency operating regions rather than isolated optimal points. Together, these results demonstrate that incorporating physical knowledge into Bayesian optimization improves the exploration and reconstruction of multidimensional high-order harmonic generation landscapes, extending its capabilities beyond locating individual optima.

summaries.en: A physics-informed Bayesian optimization framework that incorporates known scaling relations through nonlinear transformations of the search space more accurately reconstructs the multidimensional pressure-length high-order harmonic generation landscape, including extended high-efficiency regions, than conventional Bayesian optimization.
summaries.zh: 一种物理信息贝叶斯优化框架通过搜索空间的非线性变换纳入已知的标度关系，比传统贝叶斯优化更准确地重建多维压力-长度高阶谐波产生景观，包括扩展的高效率区域。
summaries.ja: 既知のスケーリング関係を探索空間の非線形変換を通じて組み込む物理情報ベイズ最適化フレームワークは、従来のベイズ最適化よりも正確に多次元の圧力-長さ高次高調波発生ランドスケープを、拡張された高効率領域を含めて再構築する。

title: Exponential Control of Adiabatic Time Reflection by Complex-Time Singularities
abstract: Nearly identical temporal switching profiles can produce very different reflections even when both have small local adiabatic measures. In a lossless dielectric, we obtain this difference by adding a weak feature that changes the complex-time singularities while preserving monotonicity, endpoints, and central slope. A perturbation bounded by $0.6\%$ of the total inverse-permittivity change raises the reflected mode amplitude from $8.02\times10^{-10}$ to $1.28\times10^{-3}$. The complex action and pole residue predict this amplitude to within $0.32\%$. Within this waveform family, deviation and monotonicity constraints select three design regimes. At fixed deviation bound, reoptimization keeps the central feature's time scale comparable to the inverse incident angular frequency. The optimal amplitude is then proportional to $1/T$ as the switching time $T$ tends to infinity. Stretching a fixed profile gives exponential suppression. Full-wave Maxwell simulations resolve the backward packet, and filtering calculations quantify its sensitivity to modulation bandwidth.

title: Intracycle Interference in Strong-Field Photoemission from a Tungsten Needle Tip
abstract: Electrons photoemitted by strong laser fields can rescatter, generating attosecond high harmonics. Spectral peaks arise from inter- and intracycle interference of coherent electron wave packets. While intercycle interference is well known, intracycle interference of plateau electrons has not been observed. We present carrier-envelope phase-resolved photoemission spectra from a nanometric tungsten needle tip driven at 1570 nm revealing such interference, supported by quantum orbit and TDSE simulations that elucidate attosecond-scale electron dynamics.

summaries.en: Carrier-envelope-phase-resolved photoemission spectra from a nanometric tungsten needle tip driven at 1570 nm reveal intracycle interference of plateau electrons, supported by quantum-orbit and time-dependent Schrödinger equation simulations that elucidate attosecond-scale electron dynamics.
summaries.zh: 在1570纳米驱动下，从纳米钨针尖获得的载波包络相位分辨光电子谱揭示了平台电子的周期内干涉，量子轨道与含时薛定谔方程模拟对此提供了支持，并阐明了阿秒尺度的电子动力学。
summaries.ja: 1570nmで駆動されたナノメートルサイズのタングステン針先端からのキャリアエンベロープ位相分解光電子スペクトルがプラトー電子の周期内干渉を明らかにし、量子軌道および時間依存シュレーディンガー方程式シミュレーションがこれを支持しアト秒スケールの電子ダイナミクスを解明する。

title: Nanostructuring Semiconductor Surfaces Using Self-Assembled Metal Nanoparticles for Optoelectronic Applications
abstract: Semiconductor nanostructures are key light-management elements because their geometry can strengthen light-matter interaction, suppress reflection, and enhance optical coupling. Yet their adoption across material platforms is constrained by lithography, multistep pattern transfer, persistent masks, and material-specific etching. Here, we introduce a lithography-free two-step strategy in which thermally evaporated self-assembled Ga nanoparticles act as self-consuming masks during Ar inductively coupled plasma reactive-ion etching. Correlated transmission electron microscopy on GaAs reveals the formation mechanism. Comparable erosion of the Ga nanoparticles and exposed substrate progressively converts Ga-capped pedestals into pure semiconductor nanocones while preserving crystalline order. Nanocone dimensions extend from tens to hundreds of nanometres, and surface coverage is tunable through Ga deposition and plasma power. The same process produces nanocones on GaP and Si and dense nanostructures on polycrystalline hybrid metal-halide perovskite without detectable PbI2 formation. During nanostructuring, the sun-weighted reflectance reaches minima of 11-15% on the monocrystalline substrates, whereas the perovskite achieves 0.5% after complete mask consumption. The approach therefore combines a self-assembled mask, its consumption, and pattern transfer in a single physical etching step, providing a simple route to light-coupling surfaces for III-V, Si, and perovskite optoelectronics.

summaries.en: Thermally evaporated self-assembled Ga nanoparticles serve as self-consuming masks during Ar inductively coupled plasma reactive-ion etching, enabling a lithography-free single-step fabrication of crystalline semiconductor nanocones on GaAs, GaP, and Si and dense nanostructures on hybrid perovskite, with sun-weighted reflectance reaching 11-15% minima on monocrystalline substrates and 0.

title: Tidal potential measured with distant optical clocks
abstract: Fibre-linked optical clocks sense tidal changes of the gravitational potential, but separating overlapping tidal components and quantifying their precision remain challenging. Using strontium and ytterbium clocks 692 km apart, we measure over 353 days a response of 0.95 (0.11) to the combined solid-Earth and ocean-loading tide and 1.01 (0.13) for the lunar semidiurnal group, and separate the lunar and solar-frequency semidiurnal contributions. A signal-to-noise model based on the actual sampling accounts for the lunar precision and guides future clock-network observations.
